item.title: Active zero day exploitation targets Palo Alto Networks EXPEL engine flaw CVE-2026-118820 for unauthenticated RCE
item.description:
Perimeter threat telemetry advisories published today warn of active zero-day attacks targeting firewalls and secure edge gateways. Remote unauthenticated threat actors exploit input validation subroutines to execute arbitrary system commands under elevated root privileges.
The emergency security bulletin covers Palo Alto Networks PAN-OS software managing Next-Generation Firewalls and Panorama appliances. The vulnerability, tracked as CVE-2026-118820 with a CVSS score of 9.8, resides within the EXPEL log parsing engine when handling external syslog telemetry streams. Unauthenticated remote adversaries transmit malformed syslog packets containing embedded shell command characters, triggering uninitialized memory parsing that executes arbitrary operating system commands with root privileges. Palo Alto Networks released emergency maintenance hotfix builds 11.2.4-h3, 11.1.2-h9, and 10.2.8-h12, confirming active wild probing targeting internet-exposed management ports.
Subverting perimeter firewall controllers and management nodes destroys network boundary protections across enterprise deployments. Because PAN-OS firewalls terminate site-to-site IPsec tunnels, manage multi-factor user authentications, and enforce core routing rules, an unauthenticated root compromise allows threat actors to disable security inspection engines, steal active session tokens, and move laterally across production subnets.
- Upgrade PAN-OS software installations immediately to emergency hotfix releases 11.2.4-h3, 11.1.2-h9, or 10.2.8-h12. - Restrict incoming syslog parsing and management web access to isolated out-of-band VLANs away from public routing. - Inspect PAN-OS system logs and process trees for unauthorized shell spawns originating from log parsing daemons. - Enable strict threat prevention profiles on management interfaces and invalidate active administrative session cookies.
Perimeter firewall controller defense relies on immediate out-of-band management isolation and rapid hotfix deployment to ensure edge security gateways remain protected from unauthenticated remote code execution exploit chains. #CodeDefence #PaloAltoNetworks #PANOS #EXPEL #ZeroDay #RCE #Firewall #PerimeterSecurity #AppSec #PatchManagement #CISA

item.title: PoC exploit published for VMware Cloud Foundation unauthenticated deserialization flaw CVE-2026-128901
item.description:
Cloud virtualization infrastructure alerts published today urge immediate security updates following public exploit code release. Remote unauthenticated adversaries can exploit Java object deserialization subroutines to execute arbitrary system code on core cloud orchestration servers.
The vulnerability, tracked as CVE-2026-128901 carrying a CVSS score of 9.8, impacts Broadcom VMware Cloud Foundation VCF and SDDC Manager deployments. The security defect resides in Java RMI object deserialization handlers processing unauthenticated remote API calls. Public proof-of-concept exploit code published today demonstrates unauthenticated remote command execution under root context by transmitting malformed serialized Java payloads over port 7080. Threat intelligence sensors report automated scanning arrays hitting exposed management consoles within hours of code availability.
Subverting central cloud virtualization orchestrators impairs private cloud security boundaries across enterprise facilities. Because VMware Cloud Foundation manages core virtual machine provisioning, hypervisor clusters, and cloud storage pools, an unauthenticated root takeover allows threat actors to manipulate virtual infrastructure, access tenant memory spaces, and compromise corporate workloads.
- Apply Broadcom security advisory VMSA-2026-0012 maintenance updates across all VMware Cloud Foundation hosts immediately. - Restrict network access to SDDC Manager and VCF API endpoints, isolating management interfaces on dedicated VLANs. - Inspect Java service process trees across Cloud Foundation nodes for unauthorized shell execution or unverified network connections. - Enforce network microsegmentation to block unauthenticated transit traffic targeting internal virtualization management ports.
Virtualization platform security demands emergency patch deployment and rigid API control plane microsegmentation to ensure private cloud hypervisors remain protected against unauthenticated deserialization exploits. #CodeDefence #VMware #CloudFoundation #SDDC #Deserialization #RCE #PoC #CloudSecurity #AppSec #PatchManagement #CISA

item.title: CISA adds Ivanti EPMM remote code execution vulnerability CVE-2026-121045 to Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog
item.description:
Federal cybersecurity authorities have updated Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog directives under Binding Operational Directive 22-01, issuing emergency patch mandates for an endpoint management platform flaw. Remote threat actors actively weaponize improper input validation routines to execute arbitrary commands across mobile management servers.
The KEV catalog addition features Ivanti Endpoint Manager Mobile EPMM vulnerability CVE-2026-121045. Unauthenticated remote adversaries transmit crafted HTTP requests to public administration interfaces, triggering command injection subroutines within backend API daemons. Cyber threat research disclosures confirm threat actors actively exploit the vulnerability to gain root execution privileges, drop web shell backdoors, and extract managed mobile device tokens and configuration records. Federal civilian agencies must complete remediation patches by early December 2026.
Subverting enterprise endpoint management servers exposes corporate mobile fleets and internal access boundaries. Because Ivanti EPMM controls mobile device enrolment, security configurations, and enterprise access credentials, an unauthenticated root compromise allows threat actors to issue malicious device policies and pivot into internal corporate networks.
- Force immediate installation of official security release builds across all self-hosted Ivanti EPMM server nodes. - Restrict public internet visibility of EPMM administration portals, placing management web interfaces on isolated out-of-band VLANs. - Inspect EPMM server file systems and API logs for unauthorized web shell scripts or anomalous process spawns. - Invalidate active administrative user session tokens and execute mandatory credential rotations across managed mobile accounts.
Enterprise mobile management defense demands immediate dependency patch execution and strict boundary isolation to ensure mobile management controllers remain protected against unauthenticated command execution exploits. #CodeDefence #Ivanti #EPMM #MobileSecurity #RCE #CommandInjection #CISA #KEV #EndpointSecurity #AppSec #PatchManagement
